narrative.title: The Vault's Lowest Alarm Gauge
narrative.scenario: A security vault stacks sealed boxes, and the control panel must flash the smallest serial number currently inside at any moment — without scanning the pile. Each panel action either drops a box, lifts the top box, reads the top serial, or flashes the minimum serial across the whole pile. Design the panel so every action answers instantly.
narrative.inputFormat: A list of operations over one stack: ["push", value], ["pop"], ["top"], or ["getMin"].
narrative.outputFormat: Return the list of values produced by every top and getMin operation, in order (push and pop produce no output).
constraints: pop, top and getMin are always called on a non-empty stack
Each operation must run in O(1)

testCases.explanation: The pile bottoms out at -3; after lifting it, the top is 0 and the minimum rises to -2.
Two pushes; the minimum never changes because 1 stays below 2 the whole time.

hintLevels: Level 1: A running minimum must be restorable when the element that set it is popped.
Level 2: Cache the minimum-so-far alongside each pushed value (or push deltas against the current minimum).
Level 3: Popping is only special when the removed element was itself the minimum — the cached pair restores the previous minimum automatically.
